questions.question: What best defines a completed transition of care?
choices: The hospital prints a discharge summary
The receiving team accepts responsibility, the patient and caregiver can perform the plan, services function, and high-risk issues have named owners
The patient leaves the building
A follow-up referral is placed without confirmation
questions.explanation: A safe transition requires closed-loop transfer of clinical responsibility, understanding, resources, services, and follow-up—not merely a discharge order.

questions.question: What is the safest medication-reconciliation method after hospitalization?
choices: Use only the discharge list
Restart every pre-admission medicine
Compare pre-admission, inpatient, discharge, pharmacy, and actual home products and explain every start, stop, dose change, duplication, and monitoring plan
Discard all older medicines without review
questions.explanation: Multiple sources plus brown-bag verification reveal intentional changes, errors, duplicates, access problems, and temporary therapies that one list may miss.

questions.question: A culture is pending at discharge. What is the most important safety action?
choices: Name who will review it, when it is expected, how the patient will be contacted, and what action threshold applies
Assume the laboratory will manage treatment
Tell the patient to search the portal daily
Wait until the next annual visit
questions.explanation: Pending results require explicit ownership, access, communication, and action planning so they do not disappear between inpatient and outpatient systems.

questions.question: Which statement about a post-discharge teach-back is correct?
choices: It tests the patient's intelligence
It is unnecessary if instructions are printed
It should ask only whether the patient understands
It asks the patient or caregiver to explain or demonstrate the plan in their own words so misunderstandings can be corrected
questions.explanation: Teach-back verifies communication effectiveness and practical ability without shaming the patient; yes-or-no questions commonly miss misunderstanding.

questions.question: Which statement about Medicare home health is most accurate?
choices: It always provides continuous custodial supervision
It may cover eligible intermittent skilled services, but it does not automatically replace continuous caregiving
It is identical to long-term nursing-home care
Every discharged patient qualifies
questions.explanation: Home-health benefits and eligibility are specific; limited skilled visits cannot meet a need for round-the-clock supervision or custodial assistance.

questions.question: An older adult is medically stable but cannot transfer, climb home stairs, prepare food, or manage oxygen. What is the safest response?
choices: Send home because vital signs are normal
Tell the family to try harder
Reassess function, home environment, caregiver capacity, equipment, and the need for rehabilitation or a more supportive setting
Schedule an annual wellness visit
questions.explanation: Medical stability does not establish functional safety; the discharge setting must match mobility, self-care, device, and caregiver requirements.

questions.question: Which medication combination error requires immediate clarification?
choices: The patient is taking both the old and newly prescribed anticoagulant after discharge
A moisturizer brand changed
A multivitamin bottle is nearly empty
The patient prefers morning dosing for an appropriate medicine
questions.explanation: Duplicate anticoagulation can cause major bleeding and demands prompt clinical assessment, regimen clarification, pharmacy communication, and patient education.

questions.question: Which statement about Transitional Care Management is correct?
choices: Billing criteria define all safe transition care
Rules never change
It applies automatically after every health encounter
CMS has specific current setting, contact, medication, visit, timing, and billing requirements, but clinical care should not be delayed when billing criteria are unmet
questions.explanation: TCM is a defined CMS service; safe clinical follow-up and escalation remain necessary regardless of whether a particular claim meets reimbursement rules.

questions.question: A patient becomes newly confused, hypotensive, and oliguric after discharge on a changed diuretic regimen. What is the best approach?
choices: Wait for the routine visit
Arrange urgent assessment for volume, kidney, medication, infection, and other causes rather than assuming normal recovery
Encourage an extra diuretic dose
Attribute it to permanent dementia
questions.explanation: Acute confusion with hypotension and oliguria may signal serious volume depletion, AKI, toxicity, or infection and requires prompt evaluation.

questions.question: How should readmissions be interpreted in transition-quality review?
choices: Every readmission proves outpatient failure
Readmissions are irrelevant
Some are medically necessary; review whether disease severity, communication, medication, access, services, or social conditions contributed
Avoid emergency referral to keep the rate low
questions.explanation: Readmission rate alone lacks context; patient safety requires necessary escalation while preventable system failures should be identified and improved.
